title: Amyotrophic Lateral Sclerosis (ALS), a Complex Interaction of Genes, Metabolism, and Environment: Precision Medicine Applied to ALS
official: Amyotrophic Lateral Sclerosis (ALS), a Complex Interaction of Genes, Metabolism, and Environment: Precision Medicine Applied to ALS
summary:
The overall objective of the study is to characterize in depth a series of ALS patients and at-risk family members to obtain an overview of the pathophysiology of the disease from its presymptomatic stages to more advanced stages. The aim is to identify new biomarkers, open up new therapeutic avenues, and promote the application of precision medicine. Specifically, the role played by genetics, microbiota, and metabolic and epigenetic changes in the development and progression of the disease will be analyzed.

To this end, three cohorts will be studied longitudinally: 100 ALS patients (including 20 with C9ORF72 expansions), 40 presymptomatic carriers of C9ORF72 expansions, and 40 controls (family members who are not mutation carriers). In all of them, motor and cognitive impairment will be characterized in depth and the following biomarkers will be analyzed: i) Neurodegeneration: serum light neurofilament; ii) Metabolism: various targeted metabolites, bioimpedance, calorimetry, fasciculations, and subcutaneous and visceral fat measured by ultrasound.

This evaluation will be repeated at 6 months in patients and at 2 years in presymptomatic carriers.

In a subgroup of 40 sporadic patients, 20 C9ORF72, 20 presymptomatic C9ORF72 carriers, and 40 controls, the following will also be performed upon recruitment, metagenomic studies in stool, untargeted lipidomics in plasma and feces, and a targeted study of genes of interest in metabolism and ALS and DNA methylation using long-read sequencing technology in blood.

Throughout the study, participants will be clinically monitored according to standard clinical practice, using survival (patients) and disease onset (carriers) as primary endpoints.

At the end of the study, the relationship between the biomarkers and microbiota analyzed will be analyzed in relation to disease progression.
criteria:
Inclusion Criteria:

* ALS diagnosis by an expert neurologist, with less than one year since diagnosis.
* Family member at risk who is a carrier of the C9ORF72 mutation.
* Family member at risk who is not a carrier of the mutation.
* Signature of informed consent.
